coverage.method: scan_ts() finds every node-redis client method call (receiver-filtered for ambiguous names such as get/set/del) in dimabot/src, dima-analytics/src, dimadb/server, dimafx/server/src and dima-hoststats/src (tests excluded); scan_rs() finds every redis::cmd/.cmd/Script::invoke_async site in dima-rust/src (unit-test modules excluded). Every site is classified into a key pattern, a Lua script, a multi-key site, or a non-key operation; unmatched sites are listed. Re-run `python3 dima-rust/tools/ledger/dragonfly_ledger.py --check`.

delegatingFiles.note: Files that obtain or type a Redis client but issue no command themselves; each was read and passes the client to helpers already covered (permissions/roles.ts, billing.ts isAiCreditsExhausted/getAiCredits, pets/tts_lane.ts) or only warms the connection.

caveats: Process attribution is static import reachability from dimabot/src/server/index.ts (api), bot/index.ts (bot), workers/cron.index.ts and each cron worker entry: "can run in", an over-approximation.
Call sites whose key comes from a variable were resolved by reading the code (file-scoped matchers and the TS_MULTI table in the generator).
Dynamic keys built by Lua from ARGV do not exist (all scripts use KEYS).
dimadb is a generic operator console: it can read/write any key; it is recorded once as dimadb.any.

queues.name: cron:jobs:queue (+ cron:jobs:dead-letter, cron:jobs:dedupe:*, cron:jobs:accepted:*)
producers: api/bot/cron via utils/cron_jobs_queue.ts enqueueCronJob: Lua ENQUEUE_DEDUPLICATED_JOB (LPUSH) or plain LPUSH (:170)
queues.consumer: cron:follow-ledger (workers/follow_ledger.worker.ts:165) BLPOP cron:jobs:queue 5 s on the shared command connection; only job "follow-ledger-sync" is processed, others RPUSHed to cron:jobs:dead-letter
queues.semantics: LPUSH + BLPOP = LIFO for fresh jobs; requeues go to the tail (RPUSH). No processing list: a crash after BLPOP loses the job (dedupe marker expires). Channel lock cron:follow-ledger:running:{c}.

queues.name: cron:stream-memory:queue → cron:stream-memory:processing (dead: cron:stream-memory:dead-letter)
producers: enqueueCronJob durable path → durable_cron_jobs.ts PUBLISH_DURABLE_CRON_JOB (LPUSH if LPOS miss)
queues.consumer: cron:stream-memory (workers/stream_memory.worker.ts:372) BLMOVE queue processing LEFT RIGHT 5 s via sendCommand on the shared connection, then LREM processing 1 raw on success
queues.semantics: Head pop after LPUSH = LIFO. Recovery RPOPLPUSH processing → queue (≤100) between jobs while holding worker:stream-memory:lock. Mongo intent claim is authoritative; Redis is transport.

queues.name: cron:clip-recommendations:queue → :processing (dead: :dead-letter)
queues.consumer: cron:vod-clip-recommender (workers/vod_clip_recommender.worker.ts:296) BLMOVE queue processing RIGHT LEFT (FIFO), ack/requeue/dead-letter via owner-fenced Lua (CLIP_CLAIM_SCRIPTS)
queues.semantics: Every transition is fenced by worker:clip-recommendations:lock value; recover = RPOPLPUSH processing → queue.

queues.name: cron:ai-usage-receipts:queue → :processing (dead: :queue:dead, attempts: :queue:attempts:{sha256})
queues.consumer: rust:ai-usage-receipts (dima-rust/src/workers/ai_usage_receipts/queue.rs:164 claim Lua LPOP→RPUSH processing; complete/fail Lua). TypeScript consumer code still exists in ai_usage_queue_health.ts helpers.
queues.semantics: FIFO. Poll (no blocking op). Max 3 attempts (1 for invalid JSON). Startup reclaim RPOP processing → LPUSH queue. Single consumer guarded by worker:ai-usage-receipts:lock.

queues.name: cron:ai-usage-backfills:queue → :processing (dead: :dead, dedupe: :dedupe:v{n}:{c}:{cust})
queues.consumer: cron:ai-usage-backfill (claimUsageJob → LPOP/RPUSH Lua, poll loop) guarded by worker:ai-usage-backfill:consumer
queues.semantics: FIFO; startup RECLAIM LPOP processing → LPUSH queue; dedupe key released by owner-checked DEL with value job.id.

queues.name: observability:v1:inbox → observability:v1:processing
producers: every TS process telemetry.ts flushTelemetry (Lua ENQUEUE: LPUSH, LTRIM 0 99, overflow INCRBY)
queues.consumer: dima-analytics/src/index.mjs:142 LINDEX processing 0 else LMOVE inbox processing RIGHT LEFT; LREM processing 1 raw after ingest
queues.semantics: FIFO, bounded to 100 batches, single consumer.

queues.name: twitch:follow-defense:queue (+ :queue:data:{eventId})
queues.consumer: cron:follow-defense processFollowDefenseQueue (utils/follow_defense.ts:497) ZRANGEBYSCORE 0 now, first 50; ZREM+DEL on success, ZADD now+5000 on failure
queues.semantics: at-least-once; no lease (single worker lock worker:follow-defense:lock).

queues.name: twitch:moderation:banmod:restore:queue (+ :data:{jobId})
queues.consumer: same file :114 ZRANGEBYSCORE 0 now; claim by ZREM result == 1
queues.semantics: ZREM-as-claim gives single delivery across processes.

queues.name: follow:defense:baseline:due
queues.consumer: rust:follow-defense-baseline (workers/follow_defense_baseline.rs:285 ZRANGE 0 0 WITHSCORES; rescore +60 s before work, +3600 s after)
queues.semantics: TS processDefenseBaseline is dead code; Rust owns consumption.

queues.name: ast:timers:pending (+ ast:timers:job:{id}, ast:timers:channel:{c})

TS sends the full script text with EVAL each call (no SHA dependency). redis-rs Script hashes the text it sends; Dragonfly caches by SHA1 of the exact text.

redisDifferences.detail: Both node-redis 5.12.1 (default) and redis-rs 1.7.1 (default) speak RESP2 to Dragonfly. Do not switch the Rust side to RESP3 without re-checking every reply type below (maps, doubles, nulls, push messages).

node-redis returns a null-prototype object (field order = reply order); missing key → {} (code checks data.id / account.id). redis-rs → HashMap (order lost) or Vec of pairs; missing key → empty map. Code that serializes the result (twitch:accounts) must keep order.

GET/HGET/LPOP/LINDEX/GETDEL of a missing key → null (TS) / Nil → Option::None (Rust). EVAL: Lua nil or false → null; a Lua table stops at the first nil (so {nil, x} returns []). Scripts returning nil: ast_timer CLAIM, aiusage.claim, CLIP recover. BLPOP/BLMOVE timeout → null.

EVAL turns Lua numbers into integer replies (fractions truncated) — TS gets a JS number, code wraps with Number(). Scripts mixing types: TAKE {allowed, used} integers; tts POP {id, payload, session} strings; desktop finish/retire/expire {revision integer, raw string}; follow-defense scripts {0|1, string}; desktop.readSlot {raw, revisionString}; rust BACKLOG_HEALTH {count, scoreString}. Rust must decode heterogeneous arrays (redis::Value or tuples). SISMEMBER/EXISTS/SETNX-style replies are integers in RESP2 (node-redis v5 returns numbers: code compares === 1).

SET NX returns "OK" or null (TS compares === "OK" or truthiness; command_cooldown_write.ts:33 uses !await). Rust: Option<String>. node-redis option objects map to: {EX}, {PX}, {NX:true, EX|PX}, {KEEPTTL:true} (dimadb), PXAT only via Lua.

node-redis v5 stringifies number arguments with JS Number#toString (set(key, Date.now()), set(key, 0), zAdd scores, hIncrBy increments, EX values). eval({arguments}) must already be strings (code uses String()). A non-integer hIncrBy increment fails with ERR; JS integers above 2^53 lose precision. Rust: pass i64/u64 or pre-formatted strings.

node-redis multi().exec() returns the reply array (site_agent/store.ts:253 and docs_assistant.ts:158 consume results positionally); a command error rejects exec with a MultiErrorReply. Dragonfly executes MULTI atomically across shards. Rust: redis::pipe().atomic() and decode the tuple in the same order.

Dragonfly runs scripts atomically only over declared KEYS; undeclared key access fails unless --default_lua_flags=allow-undeclared-keys (TS comments: tts_session.util.ts:3, ast_timer_runtime.ts:127). All TS scripts declare their keys (optional KEYS[2]/[3] are passed or omitted). Rust library scripts IDS (SSCAN) and HASH_IDS (SCAN inside Lua) in twitch_streamers/adapters.rs need verification on Dragonfly before use. redis.call("TIME"), cjson, redis.pcall + redis.error_reply are used and supported.

TS always sends EVAL with the full text. redis-rs Script::invoke_async uses EVALSHA and falls back to EVAL on NOSCRIPT, but explicit pipe().cmd("EVALSHA") in the Rust library (plan_cache_fence.rs:535, twitch_streamers/adapters.rs:433) fails after a Dragonfly restart/SCRIPT FLUSH unless the scripts are loaded first.

BLPOP (follow-ledger) and BLMOVE via sendCommand (stream-memory LEFT→RIGHT, vod-clip RIGHT→LEFT) run on the shared node-redis connection. In Rust, a ConnectionManager clone shares one multiplexed socket: a blocking command would stall every task of that process; use a dedicated connection with no response timeout (as redis.rs documents).

node-redis needs a duplicate connection in subscriber mode; the callback gets (message, channel) strings. redis-rs ConnectionManager cannot SUBSCRIBE under RESP2: use client.get_async_pubsub() on a dedicated connection and re-subscribe after reconnect (node-redis does it automatically).

KEYS is used on hot paths (TwitchStreamers cache read twitch_streamers.class.ts:99, roles.ts:251-320, tts_queue.handler.ts:1187,1288, speech.ts:21, clip_queue.handler.ts:290, cache.ts:58). scanIterator in node-redis v5 yields arrays of keys per page (site_agent/cleanup.ts:13 handles both). Dragonfly KEYS/SCAN glob semantics match Redis; SCAN COUNT is a hint.
clip_queue.handler.ts:317 calls DEL "twitch:*:clip:processing" — a literal key, so it deletes nothing. Keep or fix consciously; do not assume it clears locks.
XADD with MAXLEN ~ 4000: node-redis TRIM option; Dragonfly may trim exactly. XRANGE replies → [{id, message:{e}}] in TS, Vec<StreamId> in redis-rs.

zRangeWithScores returns JS numbers parsed from score strings; redis-rs f64. ZADD LT (follow_defense_baseline.ts:34) needs Redis ≥ 6.2 semantics (supported by Dragonfly). zPopMin returns {value, score} or null.

Many TS writes do SET then EXPIRE (logger.ts:82-83, evaluator.ts:491-501, auth.middleware.ts:45-46,166-173, metrics). A crash between leaves a key without TTL. A Rust port may use SET EX (the Rust logger already does) — semantically compatible.

dima-analytics parses INFO (used_memory, used_memory_rss, maxmemory, evicted_keys, expired_keys, keyspace_hits, keyspace_misses, connected_clients, instantaneous_ops_per_sec); Dragonfly reports these names but values/semantics can differ from Redis.

rules: Key names are an API: reuse the exact templates in `keys[]`, including legacy duplicates that are still read or deleted ({c}:ai:exhaust, {c}:follows:count, {c}:commands:{cmd}, twitch:{c}:commands:{cmd}, streamers:by:name, {c}:channel:editors, {c}:admins*). Never introduce a new key that a TS process must honour (the Rust library keys streamers:directory:*, locks:streamers:reconcile are unknown to TS).
Use the same Lua script semantics (copy the source text verbatim, keep KEYS order and ARGV meaning); declare every key a script touches (Dragonfly).

Every fenced write goes through the same fence: plan fence (WRITE/ACCEPT/SYNC/INVALIDATE scripts), owner-checked lock release/extend, site-agent CAS/lease, desktop slot fence, keyword revision. Never write a fenced key with a plain SET.
Value encodings: JSON written by Rust must parse to the same shape TS expects (camelCase names, omit absent optionals, numbers as numbers, booleans as strings in hashes where TS uses "true"/"false").
Byte-sensitive items (`byteSensitive[]`) must be produced bit-exact; values removed by value (LREM/LPOS) must be the raw bytes read, never re-serialized.
Readers must tolerate Lua cjson re-encoding (key order, "\/", exponent numbers, {} for empty arrays) and JS formatting (integral floats without ".0").
TTL policy: keep the same TTL source (EX vs PX vs PXAT, refresh-on-write vs set-once) because other processes rely on expiry for lock recovery and cache freshness.

Queues: keep producer/consumer direction (LPUSH+head-pop LIFO for cron:jobs and stream-memory, FIFO elsewhere), processing lists, dead-letter targets, attempt limits and the single-consumer worker locks; only one consumer implementation (TS or Rust) may run per queue at a time unless the lock is shared.
Pub/Sub payloads are JSON strings; PubSubManager adds a numeric "timestamp" field. Subscribers in Rust need a dedicated pub/sub connection and must re-subscribe after reconnect.
Connections: one multiplexed command connection per process; separate dedicated connections for blocking commands, pub/sub and telemetry (telemetry must not queue offline or retry).
RESP2 only; decode EVAL replies as heterogeneous redis::Value where scripts mix integers and strings.
When a TS function is ported, port all its call sites listed in `keys[].writers/readers/luaRefs` for that process; a key is migrated only when every writer and reader is accounted for.
